Peer normalization

framework §4

Each raw metric is scored against the peer group for this industry and size band, so the model reads position relative to comparable businesses rather than the raw figure.

Standardization applied to every continuous input

Expected transaction value

framework §8

The reported value is the fitted BIZCOMPS equation: log sale price on earnings, revenue, margin, year and a six-digit industry effect, median-calibrated, then placed inside the measured residual spread by the quality inputs. The turn-by-turn build in the table is the old judgment stack — kept so the direction of each adjustment stays visible, but it does not move the value.

Multiple build and resulting value
Anchoring — what the ask does to the price actually achieved

Probability of closing

framework §5–7

The reported probability is a published base rate times a price-gap penalty — it conditions on deal size and asking gap only. The contribution chart below is the judgement logistic that this replaced: it is kept because the direction of each variable is defensible and it shows what the model would weigh if the coefficients had ever been estimated. It does not move the number above.

Reported probability — base rate and gap penalty
Nonlinear terms currently active (§7)

Time to close

framework §9

The reported median is a published size-band lookup — no source publishes deal-level durations, so there is no hazard model to fit. The Weibull below is drawn only to give the curve a shape; its scale is re-solved so the median lands exactly on the published band median, and its tails carry no evidence.

Scale re-solved to the published band median

Buyer universe

framework §10–12, §20

Every buyer archetype is placed by how well it fits this company and what it could justify paying. Size is the chance that buyer engages; brightness is the chance it closes.

Buyer-specific value and synergy
Competitive effect of a deeper buyer pool

Sensitivity

framework §13

Partial derivatives computed numerically at this company's current position, for two different questions. Left: what the business supports. The fitted BIZCOMPS equation prices earnings, revenue, margin and sector; the nine quality inputs move value only by placing the business inside the fitted residual spread, so their size is measured but their placement is judgment. The ask and the buyer pool cannot change what a business supports, so they are absent here. Right: what the seller should expect to receive — closing probability times the realised price, the quantity the optimiser maximises. Every lever reaches it, but through the price gap and the ask ceiling, so the two columns can disagree, and when they do the right-hand one is the one a seller banks.

What the business supports  ∂V/∂xᵢ

Asking price moves the realised price through anchoring, up to the ask itself, while moving the closing probability the other way. The two pull against each other, which is what gives expected proceeds an interior optimum.

What the seller can expect  ∂E[proceeds]/∂xᵢ

Central-difference estimator used for each derivative

Value gap and interventions

framework §14–17

Each intervention is re-run through the full model rather than added as a flat premium, so overlapping fixes do not double-count. Cost scales with company size.

Value gap if every value-adding change is made
—
Value gap

ΔValue is the change in what the business supports. ΔE[proceeds], ΔPC and ROI are measured on top of a free reprice to the model-supported range, because at an unchanged ask the ask itself caps the price and the improvement is not collected.

Return on an individual intervention

Budget optimizer

framework §18–19

Exhaustive search over every combination of interventions that fits the budget. The two objectives can disagree — maximizing price is not always the same as maximizing the seller's overall outcome.

If you need to sell — maximize expected proceeds
—
If you can walk away — maximize overall outcome
—

Where these parameters come from

Every number the console produces carries one of three badges. Fitted means a regression was run against observed transaction outcomes and the error is measured. Aggregate means a published summary statistic was read off, so the number is real but can only respond to what the publisher tabulated. Judgement means a person picked it and no data constrains it. These tables are generated from the live model constants, so they cannot drift out of step with what the console actually runs.
